answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by fingerprinting submissions and collapsing near-duplicates: answers are hashed into overlapping fragments and compared against the ledger, so a template submitted under fifty accounts earns credit once, the rest discarded as copies. Mass-produced canned text becomes worthless, while distinct writing clears the filter. A sybil farm cannot bulk-harvest rewards by cloning one clever answer; it must write a hundred originals, exactly the work it avoided. The ledger becomes an ivory archive, a haven for real voices, where umber clones fade into a smudge.
